references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: This is the ordinary quotient ring by an ideal. Distinct specific features of this occurrence (prime ideal, polynomial base ring, local ring, square-zero ideal or powers) remain in its mathematical source. It is not a general quotient module or a quotient topology.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: isomorphism of S-schemes X and Y for a fixed base scheme S, consisting of mutually inverse scheme morphisms commuting with their structure morphisms to S; in this source S=Spec(R).
references.reason: An isomorphism respecting a base scheme is reusable independently of a closed-subscheme presentation, and is stronger than mere homeomorphism or arbitrary scheme isomorphism.
references.matching_note: Retain the base S and distinguished structure maps; compare with scheme-category isomorphism candidates in the eventual global audit.

references.context: Sheaf theory: stalk F_x of a sheaf F on a topological space X at x, the filtered colimit of sections F(U) over open neighborhoods U of x with restriction transition maps; for the structure sheaf O_X of a scheme the stalk is a local ring.
references.reason: The stalk construction is reusable in sheaf theory and explains why the local rings O_{X,x} control reducedness pointwise; it is not just the entire sheaf or a global section ring.
references.matching_note: Compare scheme local-ring and local-ring-of-stalk meanings, but retain sheaf neighborhood colimit construction.

references.disposition: The definition requires every local ring to be reduced; a single reduced stalk is insufficient.
